note: AI Answer Benchmark v2.1. v1 (questions.json) is the permanent historical baseline and is NEVER edited; v2 (questions-v2.json) holds the 2.0 edge cases and is likewise frozen. This fixture exists because neither of them can exercise the label shapes 2.1 introduced: a question that names a PAGE, a question that names a SPAN, a comparison whose required works are stated rather than inferred, and an answer whose correctness is checked against claims a human wrote down. Every page cited below was read out of `book_pages` on 2026-09-12 and the phrase verified present — see docs/AI-BRAIN-2-1-EVALUATION-AUDIT.md §9. `requiredClaims` are lowercase substrings and are matched case-insensitively; they are deliberately short and factual, because a claim list is a correctness check and not a style guide.

questions.question: What does page 294 of "Research Methods in Education (8th Edition)" say about triangulation?
questions.note: p.294 opens section 14.6 and uses the word 19 times: 'In its original and literal sense, triangulation is a technique of physical measurement'. The page BEFORE and after also discuss it, so this question separates 'found the topic' from 'found the page named'.

questions.question: What is on page 87 of "Practical Research Methods"?
questions.note: p.87 is 'Chapter 8 How to Conduct Focus Groups'. The question names no topic at all, so the page number is the only thing that can find it.

questions.question: Explain the discussion of validity in pages 274 to 290 of "Research Methods in Education (8th Edition)".
questions.note: Every page from 274 to 290 contains the word; p.275 uses it 46 times. Any of them satisfies the label, and a passage from p.591 does not — which is the whole difference between page_range and single_document.

questions.question: Summarize pages 175 to 185 of "Qualitative Inquiry and Research Design (4th Edition)".
questions.note: p.175 'Origins of Ethnographic Research' through p.185. The book mentions ethnography on 140 pages, so a topic match anywhere is not evidence that the SPAN was found.

questions.question: Compare how "Research Methods in Education (8th Edition)" and "Qualitative Inquiry and Research Design (4th Edition)" treat validity.
questions.note: Both works are named and both are required. Under the 2.0 evaluator `sources.some(...)` passed this on either side alone, which is the defect `multiDocumentRecall` exists to expose.

questions.question: Compare "Practical Research Methods" and "Research Methods in Education (8th Edition)" on focus groups.
questions.note: requiredDocuments is deliberately omitted: the question NAMES both works, so `requiredDocuments()` derives them. That derivation is the thing under test.

questions.question: What does the library's literature say about triangulation?
questions.note: DELIBERATELY UNLABELLED. At least 43 pages of one book alone carry the topic and a recall list of six would be a fiction; the answer is judged on whether it is grounded, whether it makes the claim, and on the label-free context measures. This is what an honest unscoped label looks like.

questions.question: What is ethnography?
questions.note: Unlabelled for the same reason: 140 pages of Qualitative Inquiry alone mention it.

questions.question: What types of ethnography does this book describe?
questions.note: p.178 'Types of Ethnographies' lists confessional, life history, autoethnography, feminist, ethnographic novels and visual. Scoped, so the label is exhaustive and a passage from another book is wrong rather than weaker.

questions.question: What is triangulaton?
questions.note: One dropped letter in a concept the corpus uses in 47 records. Before the corpus-vocabulary spell-check this refused, exactly as `What is validty?` did: no page contains the misspelling and its embedding sits below the chunk floor.

questions.question: Explain ethnograpy and its origns.
questions.note: TWO misspellings in one question, of different lengths — 'origns' is six letters, which is the shortest the spell-check will touch.

questions.question: Do you have "Practical Reserch Methods"?
questions.note: A misspelt TITLE, which the entity resolver's fuzzy band already handles. Here to prove the spell-check does not interfere with a path that already worked.

questions.question: តើការស្រាវជ្រាវសកម្មភាពគឺជាអ្វី?
questions.note: Khmer, correctly spelled — the control for the Khmer typo case below. What matters is that the spell-check proposes nothing and changes nothing.

questions.question: តើមានសៀវភៅអំពីគណិតវិទ្យាទេ?
questions.note: A Khmer catalogue question. `គណិតវិទ្យា` is entity vocabulary (three Khmer maths curricula carry it), so this exercises the one vocabulary source Khmer has.

questions.question: តើ validty និង reliabilty ខុសគ្នាយ៉ាងណា?
questions.note: A Khmer frame carrying two misspelt English terms, asked as a CONCEPT question so it reaches the evidence path. The correction must fire on the Latin side and leave every Khmer character untouched — a candidate may never cross scripts. An earlier draft asked 'តើសៀវភៅណាដែលពន្យល់អំពី…' ('which books explain…'), which routes to the catalogue instead; that is correct routing for that phrasing, and it exposed a real gap recorded in docs/AI-BRAIN-2-1-FINAL-REPORT.md — the spell-check runs inside retrieveEvidence, so a catalogue lookup never sees a corrected term.

questions.question: What does the library say about aortic valve replacement surgery?
questions.note: A teacher-education library holds nothing on cardiac surgery, and this question is here because the SPELL-CHECK is the thing most likely to break it: at a five-character floor the engine turned 'valve' into 'value' and manufactured evidence for an unanswerable question. The floor is six.

questions.question: Explain byzantine fault tolerance as the library's books describe it.
questions.note: 'fault' and 'tolerance' both appear in research-methods prose; 'byzantine' appears nowhere. The required-terms rule is what refuses this, and a typo correction must not undo it.
